title: Night refuge in the jungle and the Mughal use of civilians

blocks.text: As darkness did descend, the Singhs finally gained a little shelter in the jungle while the Mughal camp drew back for the night. That pause gave the fugitives a few hours to breathe, but it did not restore the strength of men already fatigued, famished and naked from continuous fighting and flight.

At midnight they moved again, only to find the hunt renewed as Mughal detachments closed in on the forest routes. The Singhs realized that desertion and escape alone would not avail, so they fought in bursts while trying to reach a bigger patch of jungle where pursuit might be blunted.

The Mughals answered by widening the chase beyond their own regular troops. They called the public with a beat of drum, armed villagers and camp followers, and drove these auxiliaries into the brush so the Sikhs could be flushed from cover even when the main army could not see them directly.
